subject: Borealis5b elevated 5xxs — progress update & post-incident plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@boreal.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2029 22:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial notice — Borealis5b observed elevated 5xx rate

Liz —

Quick heads-up from our monitoring: starting ~21:45 PDT we've observed an uptick in 5xx responses for the Borealis5b model serving your account (matched by your tenant routing). Error rate peaked around 8% for short windows and has been impacting both streaming and non-streaming generation paths.

What we know so far: 
- Scope: requests routed to borealis5b (v20290710).
- Symptom: intermittent 5xx and occasional request timeouts; higher probability at sequence lengths >1024.
- Impact: elevated error rate and increased tail latency; estimated ~2% of your requests experienced failures during the peak window.

Immediate actions we've taken: 
- Rolled traffic to a fallback model variant (borealis5b-quant-lite) for new requests to reduce customer impact.
- Captured request/response traces and a targeted log bundle — attaching sample logs and the mitigation playbook.
- Ops team running a prioritized triage to confirm root cause and stabilization plan.

Next steps: we are continuing root cause analysis and will provide a recovery ETA within the hour. Please let us know if you'd like us to keep routing all your production traffic to the fallback model for longer.

Attachments: borealis5b-5xx-sample-logs.tar.gz (logs), borealis-mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf (ops runbook)

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
From: Liz Harper <liz.harper@boreal.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2029 22:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial notice — Borealis5b observed elevated 5xx rate

Thanks Jordan —

Appreciate the quick alert. We did see a few 5xx alerts on our side and are getting customer tickets rolling in. Please keep routing to the fallback; we cannot risk higher error rates for our customers during our peak window (23:00–02:00 PDT).

Couple of asks: 
- Can you confirm whether conversation state is preserved when requests are served by borealis5b-quant-lite? (We rely on KV continuation across turns.)
- If this requires any client-side changes, tell us now so we can pause new deployments.

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Harper
Head of Platform Engineering
Boreal AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jul 2029 23:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial notice — Borealis5b observed elevated 5xx rate

Looping in infra and runtime owners — quick summary of findings from the first triage: 
1) Memory pressure correlated with KV cache thrashing on a subset of long-context requests; likely amplified by a recent kernel tweak in the attention path (merged 2029-07-10).
2) We observed an increase in GC stalls on the host process that coincided with the 5xx bursts.
3) Fallback routing reduced customer-visible errors by ~60% but wasn't a full mitigation for long-lived streaming sessions.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (short-term): 
- Pause the kernel toggle and roll back the attention optimization on the affected fleet.
- Increase per-request KV cache eviction threshold for borealis5b to reduce thrashing.
- Enable conservative CPU affinity for hosts running streaming sessions.

I'll coordinate an infra rollback and post a status update once the rollback job completes. Jordan, confirm if you want me to schedule the rollback now (30–45 min) or wait until we align with Boreal's ops window.

— Karthik
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@boreal.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 00:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial notice — Borealis5b observed elevated 5xx rate

Liz —

Thanks for the guidance. We will keep your traffic on borealis5b-quant-lite until we confirm stability for the primary variant. To answer your KV question: the fallback model preserves the same KV interoperability semantics; there is no client-side change required. For long streaming sessions we recommend re-establishing sessions after the model switch if you notice context drift — we'll monitor and advise.

Karthik — please proceed with the rollback now. Ben, please coordinate with infra to run the rollback with a canary on 10% of the affected hosts first, then a rapid ramp if metrics look good. Jordan will update Boreal once we have signal.

— Jordan
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@boreal.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Recovery update & post-incident follow-up — Borealis5b

Liz —

Status update and next steps after the rollback: 
- What happened: A recent attention-kernel optimization introduced a pathological memory access pattern for long-context workloads on certain GPU drivers. That pattern triggered KV cache thrashing and periodic host-level GC stalls that manifested as 5xx responses and timeouts.
- What we did: Rolled back the kernel change across the affected pool (canary -> full). Increased KV eviction thresholds and adjusted CPU/GPU affinities to reduce contention. We also temporarily kept your traffic on the quant-lite fallback during the verification window.
- Current status: Error rates have returned to baseline for your tenant (measured over the last 2 hours). Streaming continuity checks show stable KV behavior on replays.

Remediation items (post-incident): 
1) Engineering: regression test for long-context sequences added to the pre-merge CI for kernel changes (owner: runtime team).
2) Release: revert the kernel optimization from the mainline branch until fixes are validated.
3) Customer: we will run a joint verification session with your team tomorrow 09:00 PDT to confirm production traffic behaves as expected and to verify metrics relevant to your SLAs. I've attached the mitigation playbook and the trimmed logs we used for triage.

We regret the disruption. As a gesture of goodwill we will provide a one-time service credit for the affected window; I'll coordinate with our billing team and follow up with a formal credit note and timeline.

Please reply if you'd like us to extend the fallback routing window or if Boreal wants additional logs/trace slices for internal postmortem.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
